claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at approximately 25 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at approximately 1000 °C.
Laser-based additive manufacturing can be used to fabricate lattice-structured HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed periodic or graded lattice will contain approximately 10–20% open porosity by volume.
A high-temperature stress-relief treatment will promote homogenization in additively manufactured HfMoTaTiZr.
A high-temperature stress-relief treatment will promote stable phases in HfMoTaTiZr at elevated temperature.
Stress relief will mitigate localized stress concentrations along the lattice struts.
An open lattice reduces component-level density by removing non-load-bearing mass.
The engineered lattice will distribute mechanical loads effectively.
Scaling the lattice-strut thickness appropriately will retain strength.
The lattice architecture will lower the overall density by approximately 10–20% relative to fully dense as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The room-temperature yield strength of lattice-structured HfMoTaTiZr will remain within ±10% of the fully dense as-cast baseline.
The room-temperature ultimate strength of lattice-structured HfMoTaTiZr will remain within ±10% of the fully dense as-cast baseline.
At 1000 °C, the yield strength of lattice-structured HfMoTaTiZr will remain within ±10% of the fully dense as-cast baseline.
At 1000 °C, the ultimate strength of lattice-structured HfMoTaTiZr will remain within ±10% of the fully dense as-cast baseline.
The proposed lattice is applicable under moderate mechanical loads from ambient temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
Performance above 1000 °C or under extreme cyclic loading has not been demonstrated.

contradictions.description: The product is described as a lattice-based configuration of 'as-cast' HfMoTaTiZr, but additive manufacturing followed by stress relief produces an as-built and heat-treated state rather than an as-cast state.

The baseline is defined as as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, while the experiment states that identical post-heat treatment will be applied to all samples; a heat-treated casting is not strictly the specified as-cast baseline.
